meta.description: Orchestrator. Resolves client config ONCE from Notion, runs Module 1, then ROUTES on the request type (pricing_only | proposal_only | full_pipeline): a price-only request runs Module 3 and replies with a quote; a proposal-only request runs Modules 2+4 (no pricing); a full request runs Modules 2 ∥ 3 then Module 4. Effective route = the request's own request_type, falling back to the client's default service_tier. Incomplete RFQs branch to a Telegram review alert. Replies are SENT (not just drafted) from the client's from_alias — demo@cifral.io for trial clients, proposal@cifral.io otherwise — as a reply inside the original RFQ thread; the per-client send_mode='draft' switch parks the reply in the mailbox instead. NOTE: after import, repoint each 'Call Module N' Execute Workflow node to the deployed sub-workflow (by name) and link credentials — including the Gmail OAuth2 credential on the 'Send Quote' HTTP Request node.

parameters.content:
## 00 — Orchestrator (identify → resolve-once → route)
**Build Envelope** reads the SENDER's email from the Gmail trigger (chat runs fall back to demo_client). **Load Client Registry → Map Client Config** matches that email to a registry row via `commercial_contact_email`, enforces `Client Status` (paused/churned rejected), and resolves `client_config` ONCE (incl. `service_tier`, `pricing_sheet_id`, and `reply_to` = the sender). **Client OK?** stops unknown/inactive senders with a **Client Rejected** admin alert. The draft/quote is addressed to `reply_to` (the original sender), never the extracted end customer.

**Sender identity & delivery.** `Build Envelope` also captures the RFQ's `threadId` and builds a `Re: <original subject>` line, so replies land **inside the reseller's own thread** (Gmail needs both to thread). `Map Client Config` derives `from_alias` from Client Status — `trial` → `demo@cifral.io`, everything else → `proposal@cifral.io` — and reads `send_mode` (`send` | `draft`, default `send`). Because the Gmail node's Send operation overwrites `From` with the authenticated address, the alias only survives the **create-draft → `drafts.send`** pair; `Send Quote?` / `Send Mode?` skip the send step when `send_mode` is `draft`. ⚠️ Both aliases must be **verified 'Send mail as' addresses** on the Gmail account before switching a client to `send`.

**Call Module 1 → RFQ Complete?**: if Module 1 flags the RFQ `incomplete`, **RFQ Needs Review** (Telegram) fires and it stops. Otherwise **Resolve Route** picks the effective route — the request's own `request_type`, falling back to the client's `service_tier` — and **Route by Request Type** (Switch) branches:
- **pricing_only** → Module 3 → **Build Quote Draft** → **Create Quote Draft** → **Send Quote?** → **Send Quote** (HTTP `drafts.send`) + Telegram (a price estimate, no document).
- **proposal_only** → Module 2 → Module 4 (document with NO pricing block).
- **full_pipeline** → Module 2 ∥ Module 3 → merge → Module 4 (full document).

Pricing inputs are entered manually and **filtered by the request's scope of supply** (phase 1 has no auto hours-estimation engine). ⚠️ After import, repoint each **Call Module N** node to the deployed sub-workflow (by name) and link Gmail/Google/Anthropic/Telegram/Notion credentials.
